value.identity: equal, constant 1, for every w and under any phase conventions: w (x) v-bar -> w v^dag is an SU(2)-equivariant isometry of V_3 (x) V_3-bar onto End V_3 with the Hilbert-Schmidt norm, and v-bar -> Theta v is one of V_3-bar onto V_3, since Theta is antiunitary and commutes with SU(2); an equivariant isometry carries the V_6-isotypic part onto the V_6-isotypic part, so ||(w w^dag)_6||_HS = ||[w (x) Theta w]_6||. A unimodular change of Theta's phase leaves the norm as it is: M8.1.2's (-1)^m is -1 times M8.12's at spin 3. Under the PDF's Condon-Shortley conventions (Appendix D, p. 34), which are M8.12's, the components agree term by term; the PDF argues the link by multiplicity one and the common value 1/924 at a coherent state (Appendix A, p. 25). Forced by the definitions, as M8.1.1's conversion identity was

inputs.slice: 19 equations in the 19 unknowns (x, lambda, c_1..c_4): grad h(x) - lambda G x - sum_i c_i G k_i = 0, |x|_G^2 = 1, and <G k_i, x - x0> = 0, where k_i = X_i x0 are the four orbit generators X_i (the phase i and the three infinitesimal rotations) applied to the start point x0: constant vectors, in both places. x0 is used exactly as given, since the slice depends on it; any basis of the same four-dimensional span gives the same solution, with c = 0

A-B.Krein: the sign of M_u on each cluster ker(S_u^2 + tau^2), relative to the metric: '+' when positive definite on every cluster, '-' when negative definite on every one, 'a+, b-' counting the clusters of each sign; a cluster on which M_u is indefinite is recorded as indefinite. A simple frequency's cluster is always definite. Where the signature has n- = 0 or n+ = 0 (the coherent orbit, the hexagon, weight 7/2, the line {7/2, -3/2}) the sign follows from the signature and is read with it
A-B.along the family: the slow flow and Krein signs at each of the four members whose complex structure is j, k, (i + j)/sqrt 2 and (i + k)/sqrt 2: 'hyperbolic', hyperbolic at all four; 'definite', elliptic at all four with M_u definite on every cluster, which a signature with n- = 0 or n+ = 0 forces, so it is read with the signature
A-B.contains: the certified enclosure of 924 r6 contains the rational the PDF names; the PDF leaves equality open
A-B.critical: the representative u is a critical point of H on the unit sphere: grad H(u) = 4 H(u) u, exactly (p. 8), in each slot from its own coefficients
A-B.degenerate: a k, r_u cell that reads 'degenerate' goes with n0 > 0 in the signature and is scored with it; 'not decided at first order' and the row's type are Theorem 4.6's, Block C's (C3)
A-B.digits: for each positive decimal Table 2 prints with an ellipsis, the certified enclosure of 924 r6 lies entirely in the interval its printed digits fix: for 215.7757925..., [215.7757925, 215.7757926)
A-B.identity: holds identically: recorded as an identity, not scored as a finding
A-B.k, r_u: equal integers: k = dim K_u, the tangent space at u of the orbit of the stationary symmetry group Gamma (p. 7: right SU(2) with the phase and charge conjugation in R4 and R5, and with Sp(1) in R2); r_u the dimension of the sigma-radical of K_u (p. 13)
A-B.percent: the bound computed exactly, then rounded up at the digits printed; equal as printed
A-B.rational: equal as reduced rationals. Where a value is computed to stated digits, as A1 and A2 may be from the quartic's definition, the sum over 2I, it passes when it agrees with the rational to the digits the task document states for it
A-B.scaling: Lemma 3.1(c), each slot computed from its own coefficients: at each census orbit R5's slow polynomial in nu, made monic, equals R4's at 256 nu/81, made monic, and the signature, k, r_u, zero multiplicity and Krein signs agree; at O1 to O3 R5's certified nu-roots are 81/256 of R4's
A-B.script: the pinned script's value (MIT c7e3f46e), not the paper's: a disagreement is read for its cause first and fails no claim of the paper
A-B.signature: the integer triple (n-, n0, n+) of M_u = Hess H(u) - 4 H(u) on N_u, the orthogonal complement of u and K_u (p. 7), relative to the metric; equal
A-B.slow flow: read from the slow polynomial in nu = s^2, its zero roots removed. Elliptic: every root a negative real; then 'simple', every root simple, or 'one double frequency', exactly one double root and the rest simple. Otherwise hyperbolic: 'one real pair', no non-real root and exactly one positive root, simple; 'real pairs', no non-real root and positive roots of total multiplicity at least 2; 'a complex quartet', no positive root and exactly one conjugate pair of non-real roots, each simple. A bare 'elliptic' or 'hyperbolic' (Table 5) is the first word alone
A-B.type: 'type (PDF)' names the theorem and item the paper applies and states its conclusion, which is the paper's and is recorded beside the score. The item's hypotheses are scored by their own rules: Theorem 4.2(b), a root of the slow polynomial off the negative reals ('slow flow', hyperbolic); (c), n- = 0, and (d), n+ = 0 ('signature'); (e), every root a negative real, every cluster Krein-definite and the zero multiplicity k + r_u ('slow flow', 'Krein', 'zero multiplicity'). (Z)'s second part, the radical along the branch, is Lemma 4.3's and stays with the paper. Along the family the item is read member by member; Theorem 4.6's rows are Block C's
A-B.zero multiplicity: the algebraic multiplicity of the zero eigenvalue of S_u, its order as a root of the characteristic polynomial of S_u (the kernel alone has dimension k at a nondegenerate orbit); where (Z) asks it, equal to k + r_u

C-E.Krein: the pair's Krein sign at v1 is the sign of gamma_u (Theorem 4.6(c)); it follows from 'gamma' and is read with it
C-E.c_g: Proposition 4.7's formula evaluated: for a simple slow group, c_g = l^T T_1 r with l^T r = 1; for a semisimple group of multiplicity m, the eigenvalues of C_ab = l_a^T T_1 r_b with l_a^T r_b = delta_ab (Proposition 4.7(b)): the octahedron's group has multiplicity 3. The values are the script's, from a 50-digit computation printed to 12 significant digits by mpmath's nstr with trailing zeros dropped, and not certified; a room's value agrees when its relative difference is below 1e-9. The PDF prints no c_g (p. 19 refers them to [SSB, § III]), so, as under 'script', a disagreement is read for its cause first and fails no claim of the paper. A pass records that the formula gives the script's value; whether it is the next-order term stays with the proofs
C-E.critical: the point is a critical point of H on the unit sphere (Block A's and B's 'critical'); Corollary 4.5 speaks of critical points
C-E.gamma: gamma_u = kappa_u^-2 (Hess R~0(u) - 6 R~0(u)) on K', relative to the metric, a multiple of the metric where the PDF says so; equal as rationals in units of R^2. V cancels, since R~0 carries R^2/V^2 (Lemma 4.4) and kappa_u = Q(u)/V (p. 8), so gamma_u is the same under any volume normalization; R~0's own values (C4's script values, V = R = 1) are not
C-E.gap: lambda_1 - lambda_0 with lambda_L = L(L + 2)/R^2, the next level over the bottom; equal as rationals in units of 1/R^2
C-E.group: the order of Gamma_u, and absolute irreducibility on K' (<chi, chi> = 1 over the reals): equal
C-E.levels: the set of levels L above the slot's bottom at which P_perp N(psi_u) has a nonzero part for generic u, from the level norms of R~0's definition, not from the t_J; a level norm counts as nonzero when it is nonzero in exact arithmetic, or above 1e-12 of the largest in floating point; equal as sets
C-E.roots: S_u's slow polynomial in nu = s^2 on the components off K', its zero roots removed: the number of roots, each a negative real and simple; equal
C-E.script: the pinned script's value (MIT c7e3f46e), not the paper's: a disagreement is read for its cause first and fails no claim of the paper
C-E.sign: R~0(u) computed from its definition, -<L_0^-1 P_perp N(psi_u), P_perp N(psi_u)>, is negative
C-E.statement: Theorem 3.7 on E_0, for each n = 0 to 5 (Table 1: the control and R1, R3, R6, R7, R8): the E_0 block of the linearization at a member, computed exactly as functions of omega, g4, c and |v|, has the printed eigenvalues with their algebraic and geometric multiplicities; a computation at sample members in floating point is recorded as a check, as the paper's own is. Off E_0 the statement is a proof's (Theorem D of [SGS, § V]) and is recorded beside the score; a room's finite-model check of it is a check
C-E.type: 'type (PDF)' names the theorem and item the paper applies; its hypotheses are scored by their own rules, and the conclusion is the paper's, recorded beside the score
C-E.zero multiplicity: the algebraic multiplicity of the zero eigenvalue of S_u; equal to k + r_u where the PDF says so
